CVE-2026-119038.title: Business::GoCardless versions before 1.01 for Perl complete redirect flows without checking the session token, letting a leaked redirect flow ID create payments against another customer's mandate
CVE-2026-119038.description:
Business::GoCardless versions before 1.01 for Perl complete redirect flows without checking the session token, letting a leaked redirect flow ID create payments against another customer's mandate.

confirm_resource takes no session token from the caller. It reads the redirect flow back from the GoCardless API and completes it with the token from that response, so the check that the flow is completed by the session that started it always passes. It then creates the requested payment or subscription against the flow's mandate. Since version 1.00, a flow that already has a mandate is returned as confirmed without being completed again, so the same ID creates a new payment on every call.

A remote attacker who obtains another customer's redirect flow ID can create payments or subscriptions against that customer's mandate.

CVE-2026-126568.title: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded MSG_PEEK buffer doubling in asn_recv
CVE-2026-126568.description:
Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded MSG_PEEK buffer doubling in asn_recv.

asn_recv peeks the socket in a loop, doubling the buffer size on each pass until a tag and length can be decoded. An inverted boolean guard ($tb || rather than $tb &&) prevents the need-more-data exit from firing once a tag byte has been decoded. When asn_decode_length returns no value because the length is absent or incomplete, no exit fires for that case either. MSG_PEEK leaves socket data unconsumed, so each re-peek returns at once while the buffer size doubles.

A single truncated BER header sent to a process calling asn_recv doubles the peek buffer until memory is exhausted. Perl's realloc failure is fatal and not catchable with eval.

CVE-2026-131216.title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) through Legacy Investigation Workbench Panel Titles in Splunk Enterprise Security
CVE-2026-131216.description:
In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the manage_all_investigations capability could store attacker-controlled script content in a legacy investigation workbench panel title. Another authenticated user could later open a legacy investigation workbench that renders the panel. The script could then run in the browser of the user who opened the workbench and expose data or actions available through Splunk Web to the user who opened the workbench.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise Security does not escape legacy investigation workbench panel titles before rendering them in Splunk Web.
For more information see Capability reference for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/capability-reference-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Review and finish existing legacy investigations in Splunk Enterprise Security…

CVE-2026-45049.title: OpenAM Session Hijacking via CDSSO
CVE-2026-45049.description: Open Access Management (OpenAM) is an access management solution. Prior to 16.1.1, the `Cross-Domain Single Sign-On` (`CDSSO`) servlet allows a logged-in user's raw OpenAM session token to be POSTed to an attacker-controlled URL. An attacker who induces an authenticated victim to visit a crafted URL can receive the session credential and potentially hijack the session. Deployments must have `CDSSO` enabled, as is common in multi-domain deployments, and exploitation is additionally gated on a non-default configuration being absent. This issue is fixed in version 16.1.1.

An unauthenticated attacker who can upload a crafted DICOM to a default MONAILabel deployment can propagate NaN or infinity values through LoadImaged, Spacingd, model inference, and output writing, causing inference failures, persistent datastore poisoning, or geometrically corrupted results. This issue is fixed in version 1.6.1.

CVE-2026-53921.title: odhcpd: Stack buffer overflow in DHCPv6 IA reply serialization (2 independent sites)
CVE-2026-53921.description: odhcpd is the DHCPv6, DHCPv4, and router-advertisement server used by OpenWrt. Prior to version 25.12, odhcpd's DHCPv6 IA response handler writes past the end of a fixed 512-byte stack buffer (pdbuf) when a single DHCPv6 REQUEST carries enough IA options to nearly exhaust the reply space. Two independent overflow sites exist in the same call chain, both reachable from the network via a single unauthenticated UDP packet. odhcpd runs as root on OpenWrt; embedded targets often lack stack canaries and ASLR, making code execution realistic. This issue has been patched in version 25.12.

CVE-2026-99552.title: ocfs2/dlm: drain join handlers before releasing module text
CVE-2026-99552.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2/dlm: drain join handlers before releasing module text

The code for a registered DLM handler must remain resident until its
last invocation finishes. dlm_unregister_net_handlers() only removes
dlm_join_handlers from the o2net registry. o2net_handler_get() takes a
kref on the wrapper, but that reference does not pin ocfs2_dlm text.
o2net_process_message() calls nh_func after dropping o2net_handler_lock.

With CONFIG_OCFS2_FS_O2CB=m, ocfs2_dlm can be loaded independently of
ocfs2_stack_o2cb while nodemanager continues handling messages from a
configured, heartbeating peer. If no dependent module or module reference
prevents normal unload, the following ordering is possible:

Receive worker Module unload
-------------- -------------
o2net_handler_get()
take wrapper kref
drop handler lock
<preempted>
dlm_exit()
unregister handlers
release DLM module text
call saved nh_func
in released module text

CVE-2026-99776.title: net/9p/usbg: clear stale client pointer on close
CVE-2026-99776.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/9p/usbg: clear stale client pointer on close

p9_usbg_close() tears down the client transport, but usb9pfs keeps
using usb9pfs->client from asynchronous TX and RX completion handlers.
A late completion can therefore dereference a client that has already
been freed during mount teardown.

Clear usb9pfs->client under usb9pfs->lock when closing the transport,
detach any pending TX request from in_req->context, and make the TX/RX
completion handlers bail out once the transport has been detached. This
keeps late completions from touching a freed or rebound p9_client.
